summary: Implemented and exercised a reusable Crew-owned DSH runtime path for the isolated final acceptance. Deterministic repository tests (426/426) and the client build pass. The official Harness runtime was reused from the Crew-owned isolated runtime at @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-rc.2; official ~/.dsh persistent files remained byte/hash unchanged and the official web Harness remained healthy on port 3080. Crew install, isolated Hub compatibility, status, and final uninstall were completed without leaving a Crew process or official-profile registration. The live worker was created and reached a genuine terminal failure with a sanitized selection trace, but could not complete because the Crew-owned profile had no authorized API key. The live policy matrix also has one real failure (I1: raw pro_reviews_flash remained true). Per protocol, Crew is left uninstalled and the overall result is BLOCKED.

tests.name: Task contract validation
tests.evidence: node .agent-workflow/validator/validate-contract.mjs task docs/agent-tasks/ACTIVE_TASK.json -> VALID TASK CONTRACT (exit 0).

tests.name: Reusable Crew-owned DSH runtime resolution and deterministic Windows invocation
tests.evidence: Targeted resolver/setup suite passed 20/20. Explicit CLI and Crew-owned runtime precedence, no-network resolution, reusable runtime provisioning, Crew DSH_HOME injection, Windows .cmd quoting, and offline status/uninstall behavior are covered. Actual runtime resolved as @deepseek-ai/dsh@0.1.1-rc.2 from Crew-owned isolated state.

tests.name: Client build
tests.evidence: pnpm run build:client exited 0; generated tracked lib/client.js was restored to the source revision and is not part of the completion diff.

tests.name: Official persistent ~/.dsh integrity
tests.evidence: Non-secret metadata and SHA-256 evidence for .credentials.yaml, settings.yaml, profiles/web/package.json, profiles/web/cordis.yml, and profiles/web/pnpm-lock.yaml matched before/after. Credential contents were never read or recorded.

tests.name: Official Harness health after runtime reuse
tests.evidence: Official default web Harness started with the Crew-owned runtime entry and default official DSH_HOME; http://127.0.0.1:3080/ returned HTTP 200. The official process was left running healthy.

tests.name: Isolated Crew install/status/uninstall
tests.evidence: Real install reported the isolated dsh-crew profile and integrations installed; final status reported DSH plugin, Codex, and Claude integrations not installed. The final uninstall path removed only the Crew-owned registration offline after the package-manager network probe was unavailable. Crew Hub port 3210 became unreachable, no Crew process remained, and official web health stayed HTTP 200.

tests.name: Crew Hub/runtime compatibility and readiness catalog
tests.evidence: Isolated Hub on http://127.0.0.1:3210 with profile dsh-crew returned HTTP 200 for runtime, ping, and models. Catalog evidence reported provider_count 1 and model_count 3.

tests.name: Genuine completed worker and sanitized selection trace
tests.evidence: A genuine job was accepted and reached terminal failed state. The observed trace selected provider deepseek-official, model deepseek-v4-flash, source preferred-default, with no sensitive fields. Completion was blocked because the Crew-owned isolated profile had no authorized API key; the official credential store was not read.

tests.name: Live max_parallel and activation boundaries
tests.evidence: Deterministic tests pass raise/lower and activation-boundary semantics. Live admission/queue behavior was not fully proven because the authorized worker credential gate prevented a completed workload.

tests.name: Adaptive routing isolated roundtrip and audit behavior
tests.evidence: Deterministic adaptive-routing coverage passes. Live isolated config enable/disable roundtrip passed and restored enabled=false, window_size=8, min_samples=2; full real warming/reorder/restart execution was not completed because worker execution was credential-blocked.

tests.name: Structured failure propagation
tests.evidence: Deterministic propagation tests and policy probes pass, and the live worker produced a sanitized terminal failure. The complete live Hub-to-client-to-attempt-to-workflow chain could not be proven without an authorized worker credential.

tests.name: Live policy matrix
tests.evidence: node scripts/live-policy-matrix.mjs -> 14/15 passed. I1 failed: review-pipeline expected raw pro_reviews_flash=false but observed raw=true. Other matrix cases and restore checks passed.

tests.name: Policy probe
tests.evidence: node scripts/policy-probe.mjs -> 13/13 passed against the local MCP surface.

tests.name: Standalone execution
tests.evidence: No explicitly authorized/Crew-owned DEEPSEEK_API_KEY was present. node scripts/smoke-real.mjs standalone exited with the expected blocked result without reading official credential files.

tests.name: macOS execution
tests.evidence: Executor is Windows; macOS-only smoke was not run.

tests.name: Final local state
tests.evidence: Because live gates were BLOCKED/FAIL, Crew was left uninstalled. The Crew-owned runtime was retained for reuse, no Crew process remained, the isolated Hub was down, and the official Harness remained healthy.

tests.name: Result validator --stamp
tests.evidence: Will be executed after this draft's final timeline is written.

blockers: The Crew-owned isolated profile had no authorized API key, so a genuine successful worker and the full live worker-dependent acceptance gates could not complete; the official credential store was not read.
Live policy matrix I1 failed because review-pipeline observed raw pro_reviews_flash=true where false was expected.
Live max_parallel, adaptive warming/reorder/restart, and the complete end-to-end failure propagation chain remain unproven because worker execution was credential-blocked.
